Campbell Valley is a rural sub-area in south Township of Langley, centred on Campbell Valley Regional Park.
The park's Nature House is at the Rowlatt Farmstead, 20285 8 Avenue, reached by the South Valley Entrance.
The park's north entrance is on 16th Avenue and its equestrian centre access is on 208th Street south of 16th Avenue.
A board sub-area label does not settle a parcel's farm, Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) or park-edge status; that is parcel by parcel.
The stock is acreage homes, hobby farms and equestrian properties, mixed with small-lot rural homes inside the same sub-area label.
The regional park itself is 535 hectares with forests, fields and wetlands, which sets the open character around these parcels.
Farm classification is property by property with BC Assessment, not an area-wide label.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley: rules that affect buyers

items.t: On ALR land, one principal residence is permitted without an Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) application, to a maximum total floor area of 500 square metres.
A secondary suite on ALR land is permitted only when located within the principal residence.
At most one additional residence is permitted on ALR land: up to 90 square metres on properties 40 hectares or less, or up to 186 square metres over 40 hectares.
Township of Langley Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) under Bylaw 6020 makes lots over 4,050 square metres ineligible, so most acreage parcels here fall outside it.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Little River Loop Trail is 2.2 kilometres with boardwalks across wetlands and little elevation gain.
The Shaggy Mane Trail is the outer perimeter trail shared with horseback riders.
The Nature House is open from Victoria Day to Labour Day, with free admission, per the park visitor information.
General property transfer tax (PTT) is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, and 3% above that, with a further 2% on residential value above $3,000,000.
Township of Langley property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty at midnight July 2, 2026 and a further 5% at midnight September 3, 2026.
Farm classification, where it applies, is applied for to BC Assessment by October 31 for the next assessment and tax year.
Access is by rural roads to 16th Avenue, 200th Street and 8th Avenue at the park entrances; no rapid transit serves this rural area.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley: risks and due diligence

items.t: Confirm ALR status parcel by parcel with the ALC map before valuing dwellings, barns or subdivision.
Verify well, septic and any mobile-home pad on the specific parcel with professionals and the Township; listing-card statements are not verification.
Check the Little Campbell River and wetland edges on the lot against Township and park mapping before planning buildings.

faq.q: What homes can an ALR parcel here have?
faq.a: An ALR parcel can have one principal residence, a suite inside it, and at most one small additional residence. The principal residence is capped at 500 square metres with no more than 1,000 square metres of fill. The additional residence is capped at 90 or 186 square metres by parcel size. Local bylaws may be stricter.

faq.q: Can I strata-title or subdivide an acreage?
faq.a: Strata titling counts as subdivision in the ALR and needs ALC permission first. Outside the ALR, subdivision still needs Township approval and a proven water supply. Confirm the parcel's ALR status before valuing any split potential.

faq.q: How do I keep farm classification after buying?
faq.a: A buyer who plans to continue farming a farm-classified property must submit the General Application for Farm Classification by that date. Income thresholds vary by operation size, starting at $2,500 for operations between 0.8 and 4 hectares.

faq.q: What trails and horse facilities are in the park?
faq.a: The park offers 29 kilometres of trails, with about 14 kilometres designated for equestrian use. Walkers, cyclists and horseback riders share the network. The park holds the Campbell Valley Equestrian Society and Campbell Downs Equestrian Centre. The Nature House sits in the heritage Red Barn at the Rowlatt Farmstead.

faq.q: Are Campbell Valley's zero figures unique among Langley sub-areas?
